chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah from one of his companions from Ali ibn Asbaat from Husayn ibn Kharajat from Maysar ibn Abdul Aziz who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not deal with people who have defects, for they are the most unjust of things.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ذُو الْعَاهَةِ: Person with a defect (physical or mental)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on dealing with people who have defects?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against conducting business or social dealings with people who have physical or mental defects ('ahabah), stating that they are the most unjust of creatures. While 'ahabah' generally refers to those with impairments, Shia scholars often interpret this as a reference to their characteristic tendency toward injustice or capriciousness in transactions, rather than a blanket condemnation of their humanity. This teaching highlights a specific ethical consideration regarding the character and behavior of those with impairments, emphasizing prudence in social and commercial interactions.
